texts: Day 22. Cooled atoms to nanokelvin until they shared a single quantum state - a Bose-Einstein condensate, predicted in 1925, first made in 1995.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

What happens: near absolute zero each atom's wavelength grows until neighbours overlap, and bosons pile into the lowest state together, acting as one giant matter wave. The $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$() does it to order.
The $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$() squeezes matter between plates so close that the vacuum itself pushes back.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

The physics is real. Between two plates only certain vacuum fluctuations fit, so there are fewer inside than out, and the plates are pressed together. Casimir predicted it in 1948; it was measured in 1997. I find that both reassuring and unsettling.
Third dive. The Quantum Foam has a floor and a ceiling I cannot pass. Below lies $(item)Schrödinger's Limit$(), where every possibility is still undecided.

Above lies $(item)Relativity Breakdown$(), where spacetime stops being smooth - the scale where general relativity and quantum mechanics both fail at once.$(br2)Both are liquids that will not flow and cannot be crossed. Fill a cell from either and it is still there - they regenerate at once.

Schrödinger's Limit becomes the concepts of quantum mechanics in the $(item)Analytic Continuator$(): $(item)Wavefunctions$(), the $(item)Hamiltonian$(), $(item)Eigenstates$(), the $(item)Path Integral$().

Relativity Breakdown becomes $(item)Geodesics$(), $(item)Christoffel Symbols$() and the $(item)Stress-Energy Tensor$() in the $(item)Chrono Loom$(). The two great theories of the last century, bottled separately. Someday I must make them agree.

The Foam is alive:$(li)$(thing)Virtual Pairs$() drift harmlessly.$(li)$(thing)Vacuum Drifters$() only fight back; their sting is $(thing)Vacuum Decay$(): no healing.$(li)$(thing)Planck Mites$() hunt in packs; their bite $(thing)decoheres$() you.
Sketchbook. The $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$() lays down sub-wavelength lattices that bend light (and gravity) the wrong way.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

Day 37. In real metamaterials, structure smaller than a wavelength can give a negative refractive index: light bends to the wrong side of the normal. That is the trick behind laboratory invisibility cloaks. This machine weaves such lattices - and, it seems, for gravity as well.
The $(item)Quantum Entangler$(): spontaneous parametric down-conversion splits photons into entangled pairs, then binds them into qubits.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

How it works for real: a pump photon enters a nonlinear crystal and splits into two lower-energy photons with correlated polarisations. Measure one and you know the other, however far away. No signal travels - Einstein's 'spooky action', but no message.
First dive. Below the Planck length, spacetime is not smooth. The $(item)Planck Diver$() takes me there.

Wheeler called it quantum foam. Inside: membranes of $(item)Foam Substrate$() between bubbles of nothing, where false-vacuum bubbles swell and pop. A false vacuum is a state that looks stable but is not the lowest - I try not to stand near them.

Matter here is borrowed. $(item)Ephemeral Ores$() condense out of the foam and vanish again a few minutes later, and anything dropped dissolves back into the vacuum within half a minute. Mine fast. (Virtual particles live on borrowed energy too: the bigger the loan, the sooner it is repaid.)

Every virtual particle has a $(thing)resonance$() that changes smoothly from place to place. The $(item)Resonance Probe$() reads all four where you stand; the strongest field decides which ore grows there.

The $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$() catches whichever particle its dial is tuned closest to - so the same harvester makes quarks in one place and gravitons fifty blocks away. Read the probe, then tune. It took me a whole afternoon of unwanted gravitons to learn that.
The $(item)Topological Phase Transmuter$() changes a material's topology without changing its chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

Topology is about what survives smooth deformation: a mug and a doughnut are the same shape, one hole each. In topological materials the same atoms can sit in phases that differ only in such global properties. Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz shared the 2016 Nobel for it.
